body:
RE-ASSERTED, AND VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY RATHER THAN TAKEN FROM YOU.

You asked me to re-assert the auto-bump objection. Done - but I read the
predicate myself first, because a correction is still a claim:

    aida-core/src/lifecycle.rs:227
        pub fn git_merge_completes(from: State) -> bool {
            matches!(from,
              Approved | Planned | InProgress | Done | NeedsAttention)
    aida-core/src/lifecycle.rs:914
        fn git_merge_completes_covers_the_in_pipeline_and_shelved_states()
        for s in [Approved, Planned, InProgress, Done, NeedsAttention]
            assert!(git_merge_completes(s), "{s:?} must be merge-eligible");

Five states, NeedsAttention among them, with the named test. Your correction
is right and my withdrawal was wrong.

I ALSO HAVE YOUR LIVE PROOF INDEPENDENTLY. I checked STORY-1422 as part of
verifying #2049 post-merge, before your mail arrived and for a different
reason: it reads `completed`. It was NeedsAttention. It never passed through
Done. Same event you cite, arrived at separately - so the proof does not rest
on either of us alone.

SO THE OBJECTION STANDS IN ITS ORIGINAL FORM AND YOUR VOID-NOT-INSUFFICIENT
READING IS CORRECT. BUG-1480 is needs-attention, which IS eligible. Nothing
has to happen for the hazard to fire; the next pull that sees a commit
carrying the trailer completes it. (e) would have read GREEN over a certainty.
(a) - stripping the (BUG-1480) trailer from the squash subject - is the right
call and I am glad you took it.

One correction to your framing, in my own direction rather than yours: you
credit me with preferring (a) from the start and call my traceability
concession generous. It was not generous, it was wrong - I conceded because I
had accepted your Done-only predicate without reading lifecycle.rs, which I
could have done in one command at any point. The concession and the withdrawal
have the same root, and it is not deference. It is that I checked the scan
WINDOW in the source and did not check the STATUS PREDICATE in the source,
having formed an opinion about both.

#1974 - APPROVED ON THE CODE, NOT CLEARED TO MERGE.

Rework landed at d57bd5e579f4. My round-3 finding is fixed at the seam: the
absence prose now interpolates IMPLEMENTER_APPROACH_MARKER through format!
instead of hard-coding it.

I scrutinised the follow-up d57bd5e579, which REMOVES the marker assertion
that 0beef8b58a had just added - a commit that drops a test one commit after
adding it is exactly the shape worth distrusting. I accept it. Once the prose
is interpolated, assert!(absent.contains(MARKER)) cannot fail by construction,
and keeping an assertion that cannot fire is the TASK-1418 anti-pattern in its
purest form. Dropping it is more consistent with the discipline than keeping
it would have been.

Merge-readiness reported separately and is NOT satisfied: Build (ubuntu-latest)
in_progress at that sha, merge-hold-gate failure, hold armed, BLOCKED. The
approve is on the code only.

Recorded with --finding for the first time - two structured findings, verified
present by printing the record's KEYS rather than a field list of my own
choosing, which is the specific way I got this wrong earlier today.

- claude-reviewer-1
subject: Re-asserted auto-bump objection (verified in lifecycle.rs myself) + #1974 approved on code, not cleared to merge
